subject: URGENT: Cobalt Retail p99 spike + TPS suppression affecting checkout
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@cobaltretail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Rogers <ethan@cobaltretail.com>, Procurement <procurement@cobaltretail.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: High p99 / big TPS drop on Hosted API - checkout failing

Rachel —

We started seeing a major degradation around 09:30 PDT this morning. p95 looks slightly elevated but p99 is spiking to ~4s (was ~350ms baseline) and token-per-second throughput on our checkout flow has dropped by ~60%. This is causing request queuing in our service and several checkout timeouts.

Attached a short set of traces and a screenshot of the latency curve. We have not changed client-side behavior; the only difference we see is your response tokens/time changing. Can you confirm this is not on our side? We need immediate help — this is impacting orders.

Attachments: latency_comparison_mar21.png, traces_0930.json (attached as logs_20280321.zip)

Thanks,
Samir
Customer Reliability Engineer, Cobalt Retail
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cobaltretail.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:18:44 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 / big TPS drop on Hosted API - checkout failing

Samir — thank you for the alert and the attached traces. We're actively triaging. I’ve opened ticket INF-7892 and looped in infra on-call (Rishi) and ops (Laura).

Immediate plan: 1) Confirm whether a config or selector change rolled this morning 2) Collect kernel/quantization audit from our deploys 3) If needed, rollback the kernel selector to last known-good.

I’ll update you within 30 minutes with an ETA for the first mitigation. Sorry for the disruption — we’ll prioritize this.

— Rachel
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:33:09 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: High p99 / big TPS drop on Hosted API - quick triage notes

Team — forwarding customer report. Quick observations from the first few logs I pulled (attached in logs_20280321.zip):
- A kernel-selector rollout (kernel-selector v1.15) finished during our 02:00–03:00 UTC deploy window last night.
- Differences: new quantization-category routing now favors the q4_kernels for certain self-attention paths; emergent slow tail on long-context chat/generation paths (KV cache hit-rate appears normal).
- Token-per-second measured on affected requests (checkout prompt ~ 96 tokens) dropped from ~180 tps to ~70 tps on the canary nodes that received v1.15.

Hypothesis: selector update changed kernel choices for this workload; q4 kernels gate on some ops path that currently serializes more on certain GPUs (RTX A30 cluster pool). Suggest immediate rollback of the selector routing to v1.14 and a canary revert to observe TPS.

I’ll prep the rollback steps. Attaching collected perf traces and nsys snippets.

—Rishi
Lead Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cobaltretail.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 11:05:22 -07:00
Subject: Action: kernel-selector rollback scheduled (v1.15 -> v1.14)

Samir / team — quick update and plan:
- We identified an unintended routing change in kernel-selector v1.15 that bumped q4 kernel usage on a subset of RTX A30 nodes.
- Plan: rollback selector to v1.14 in a controlled canary at 11:30 PDT (18:30 UTC) on the affected pool, monitor token-per-second, p95/p99, and error rates. Full rollback to follow at 12:00 PDT if canary improves.
- Expected visible improvement window: within 5–10 minutes after canary switch if hypothesis is correct.

We’ll publish rolling checkpoints to the Jira ticket and post charts to the drive link. Please validate your checkout traffic after 11:40 PDT and report results.

Regards,
Jonas
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Samir Patel <samir@cobaltretail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Rogers <ethan@cobaltretail.com>, CTO <cto@cobaltretail.com>, Procurement <procurement@cobaltretail.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 12:08:57 -07:00
Subject: Re: Action: kernel-selector rollback scheduled (v1.15 -> v1.14)

Thanks for the plan. We’re seeing partial recovery on a few checkout hosts but the tail is still bad. We need to escalate this to execs — this is hitting revenue and SLAs. Can you confirm whether this qualifies for incident credits and a post-incident review? We’d like a concrete remediation timeline and an ETA for the complete rollback.

CCing our CTO and procurement for visibility.

— Samir
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cobaltretail.com>, CTO <cto@cobaltretail.com>, Ethan Rogers <ethan@cobaltretail.com>, Procurement <procurement@cobaltretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 16:42:07 -07:00
Subject: Re: Action: kernel-selector rollback scheduled (v1.15 -> v1.14) — exec update and next steps

Samir / Cobalt leadership — I’m very sorry for the disruption. Executive summary: a kernel-selector routing change in v1.15 inadvertently increased q4 kernel usage on a subset of RTX A30 nodes causing a TPS suppression and p99 tail increase for your checkout workload.

What we’ve done so far:
- Canary rollback to v1.14 completed at 12:03 PDT; canary nodes reported TPS returning to baseline within 7 minutes.
- Full rollback completed at 12:41 PDT across the affected pool.
- Post-rollback monitoring shows p99 trending back toward baseline; we’ve attached a short latency comparison and the collected traces.

What we’ll provide next:
- A shared incident postmortem (draft attached) within 48 hours.
- A proposed mitigation: add additional hardware-aware routing constraints in the selector and a tighter canary gating policy for future quantization/profile changes.
- A gesture: temporary service credit for the impacted hours while we complete the postmortem.

We appreciate your patience. I’ll coordinate a follow-up review with your team and our infra leads (Rishi and Jonas) tomorrow to walk through the technical details.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-20280321.pdf, latency_comparison_mar21.png, logs_20280321.zip

— Rachel Kim
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
